note: Draft 1 — the text every critic/v1.* verdict is about. Reconstructed by the translator from the session after the first edits to prayed.json had begun (the keep-every-draft rule arrived mid-revision); its resolved text was checked to be identical to prayed.v1.vos.json, the flat file the critics actually read.

verses.90:1: Quem habita {adjutorio} do Altíssimo, * na proteção do Deus do céu {commorabitur}.
verses.90:2: Dirá ao Senhor: Vós sois o meu {susceptor} e o meu refúgio: * {deusmeus}.
verses.90:3: Porque {ipse} me livrou do laço dos caçadores, * e da palavra áspera.
verses.90:4: Com {scapulis} {obumbrabit}: * e sob as suas {pennis} esperarás.
verses.90:5: A sua verdade te cercará com um escudo: * {timebis},
verses.90:7: Cairão mil ao teu lado, † e dez mil à tua direita: * mas de ti não se aproximará.
verses.90:8: {verumtamen} com os teus olhos contemplarás: * e verás {retributionem} dos pecadores.
verses.90:9: Porque vós sois, Senhor, a minha esperança: * {posuisti}.
verses.90:10: O mal não chegará a ti: * e o flagelo não se aproximará {tabernaculo}.
verses.90:11: Porque {mandavit}: * para que te guardem em todos os teus caminhos.
verses.90:13: Andarás sobre a áspide e o basilisco: * e {conculcabis} o leão e o dragão.
verses.90:14: Porque esperou em mim, eu o livrarei: * eu o protegerei, porque conheceu o meu nome.
verses.90:15: Clamará a mim, e eu o escutarei: ‡ com ele estou na tribulação: * eu o {eripiam} e o glorificarei.
verses.90:16: Eu o encherei {longitudine}: * e lhe mostrarei a minha salvação.

decisions.why: The Latin follows the LXX (ἐν βοηθείᾳ, 'in the help'), not the Hebrew 'in the secret place / shelter'. Matos Soares 1932 leaves the Vulgate here ('à sombra do Altíssimo'), so he is no guide; DRB has 'in the aid', pt-PT 'no auxílio'. The word is glossary-grade: adjutórium / adjútor recur all over the psalter and open every Hour (Deus, in adjutórium meum inténde).

options.label: no auxílio
options.note: Draft. Plain, current, and leaves 'ajudar / ajuda' free if adjuváre needs a different word.

options.label: na ajuda
options.note: Cognate of adjutórium and the plainest word, but 'habitar na ajuda' sounds thinner than 'habitar no auxílio'.

decisions.why: commorári is 'to tarry, abide, sojourn, stay' (L&S); LXX αὐλισθήσεται is 'will lodge, pass the night'. The Latin uses a different verb from hábitat in the first colon, so the Portuguese should too.

options.label: permanecerá
options.note: Draft: 'abide' (so DRB). Five syllables, which keeps the colon near the Latin's fifteen.

options.label: morará
options.note: Echoes the -mor- of the Latin by sound and is plainer, but leaves the colon four syllables short and sits close to 'habita'.

options.label: descansará
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT: nearer the Greek 'lodge for the night' than the Latin verb.

decisions.why: suscéptor (ἀντιλήμπτωρ) is 'one who takes up, a guardian, protector' — L&S cites this verse. It recurs often (3:4, 17:3c, 41:9, 45:8 = 45:12, 53:6, 58:10, 58:17–18, 61:3, 88:27, 118:114, 143:2 in DO's numbering), and must not collide with protéctor, which the psalter also uses constantly; prótegam / protectióne stand in this very psalm.

options.label: amparo
options.note: Draft. 'Amparar' is what suscípere does (take up, hold up), and 'o meu amparo' is said of a person in current Portuguese. Cost: an agent noun becomes an abstract one, like the refúgium beside it.

options.label: defensor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. An agent noun, but it adds the idea of fighting, which suscéptor does not have.

options.label: protetor
options.note: DRB 'protector'. Refused as the text: it would make suscéptor and protéctor one word across the psalter.

decisions.why: The man turns from 'es tu' to 'in eum' inside one sentence, and 'Deus meus' hangs between the two: a third predicate (you are my upholder, my refuge, my God) or a nominative left hanging before 'I will hope in him'. The Latin does not subordinate; MS1932 and pt-PT do ('em quem esperarei').

options.label: o meu Deus, nele esperarei
options.note: Draft. Keeps the loose syntax and the jump to the third person; with the article it can be heard either as the third predicate or as the hanging subject, as in the Latin.

options.label: o meu Deus, em quem esperarei

forms.deusmeus: o meu Deus, em quem esperarei

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT: smoother, but the relative clause is not in the Latin and settles the syntax.

options.label: meu Deus, esperarei nele
options.note: Without the article it sounds like a vocative followed at once by 'nele' — the harshest reading of the Latin, and it breaks the working rule of article + possessive.

decisions.why: ipse (αὐτός) is emphatic: 'he himself'. MS1932 and pt-PT have plain 'ele'. Note the Latin has the perfect liberávit (the LXX has a future), so 'livrou' stays.

options.label: ele mesmo
options.note: Draft. Renders ipse, and brings the colon to 17 syllables against the Latin's 18 (without it the colon is 3 short).

options.label: ele
options.note: MS1932, pt-PT. Lighter, but ipse goes unheard.

decisions.why: A Septuagintal image to keep: God overshadows with his shoulder-blades / back (μετάφρενα), where the Hebrew has 'pinions'. scápulæ is 'shoulder-blades; shoulders, back' (L&S).

options.label: os seus ombros
options.note: Draft, with pt-PT and DRB ('shoulders'): the plainer of two faithful words.

options.label: as suas espáduas
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Exact (the shoulder-blade, where a wing is rooted) but a word few Brazilians say.

options.label: as suas costas
options.note: The Greek μετάφρενα; but 'com as suas costas' can be heard as God turning his back.

decisions.why: obumbráre with the dative: 'to cast a shade for you'. The same verb and case stand in Lk 1:35 (virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi), so whatever is chosen here will want to match the canticle-side texts later.

options.label: te fará sombra
options.note: Draft, with MS1932 and pt-PT. Keeps umbra as a noun and the dative.

options.label: te cobrirá com a sua sombra

forms.obumbrabit: te cobrirá com a sua sombra

options.note: Fuller and familiar, but adds 'cobrir' and makes the colon far too long after 'Com os seus ombros'.

decisions.why: pennæ in the plural is 'wings' (LXX πτέρυγας), but the psalter also has alæ (16:8b sub umbra alárum, 35:8, 56:2, 60:5, 62:8b). One Portuguese word for both loses a distinction the Latin keeps.

options.label: asas
options.note: Draft, with MS1932, pt-PT, DRB. The sense; collides with alæ.

options.label: penas
options.note: The cognate and the concrete image (feathers), and it keeps pennæ apart from alæ; but 'sob as suas penas' is heard first as 'under his sorrows / penalties'. Refused for that ambiguity.

options.label: plumas
options.note: Avoids the ambiguity of 'penas' but is decorative where the Latin is plain.

decisions.latin: non timébis a timóre noctúrno, / A sagítta… a negótio… ab incúrsu, et dæmónio
decisions.why: timére a + ablative is a Hebraism through the Greek (φοβηθήσῃ ἀπό). It governs the whole of 90:6, which is chanted as a verse of its own and begins with the dependent 'A sagítta'. Two things are at stake: the repeated root timébis / timóre (kept in every option) and the fourfold anaphora of 'a', which Portuguese can keep only by changing the verb's regency.

options.label: não temerás o temor noturno, / A seta… a coisa…

forms.v6: A seta que voa de dia, † {negotio_acc} que perambula pelas trevas: * {incursu_acc}, e o demônio {meridiano}.

options.note: Draft. 'non timébis' word for word, root repeated; the preposition is grammar and yields (rule 2). 90:6 stays a dependent list, as in the Latin, now of direct objects.

options.label: nada temerás do temor noturno, / Da seta… da coisa…

forms.v6: Da seta que voa de dia, † {negotio_gen} que perambula pelas trevas: * {incursu_gen}, e do demônio {meridiano}.

options.note: Keeps both the root and the anaphora of 'a' (da… da… da… do), through the idiom 'nada temer de'; cost: 'nada' for 'non'.

options.label: não terás medo do temor noturno, / Da seta… da coisa…

forms.timebis: não terás medo do temor noturno
forms.v6: Da seta que voa de dia, † {negotio_gen} que perambula pelas trevas: * {incursu_gen}, e do demônio {meridiano}.

options.note: Keeps the anaphora but loses timébis / timóre as one root. pt-PT mixes the two constructions ('assombros nocturnos não temerás, / Da seta…').

decisions.why: A hard Septuagintal reading to keep: the LXX read the Hebrew 'pestilence' (deber) as 'thing, matter' (πρᾶγμα, dabar), and the Latin follows with negótium — 'like the Gr. πρᾶγμα, for res, a matter, thing' (L&S). What walks in the dark is left unnamed. MS1932 names it ('o inimigo'), pt-PT interprets ('a trama').

options.label: a coisa
options.note: Draft. The πρᾶγμα sense exactly, plain, and as unnamed and uneasy as the Latin.

options.label: o negócio
options.note: The cognate, and DRB's 'the business that walketh about in the dark'; but in Brazil 'negócio' is either commerce or slang for 'thing', and either way the line turns comic.

options.label: a trama
options.note: pt-PT: a plot. An interpretation of negótium, not a translation.

decisions.why: incúrsus is 'a running against, an assault, attack' (L&S); LXX σύμπτωμα is rather a mishap. The Latin keeps it apart from the noonday demon with a comma and 'et' — two terrors, not 'the assaults of the demon' (MS1932).

options.label: a investida
options.note: Draft. A rush at someone — the in-currere image — with no other sense.

options.label: o assalto
options.note: MS1932 and pt-PT ('assaltos'). Right in a dictionary, but in Brazil 'assalto' is first of all an armed robbery.

options.label: o ataque
options.note: Plainest; in everyday speech also a fit or seizure.

decisions.why: A reading to keep (LXX δαιμονίου μεσημβρινοῦ; the Hebrew has no demon). The only question is the adjective. checks.py flags 'de dia' († colon) against 'do meio-dia' (final) as a rhyme inside the verse.

options.label: do meio-dia
options.note: Draft, with MS1932 and pt-PT. Plain. The echo dia / meio-dia is the Latin's own (die / meri-diáno is the same root), so it is accepted.

options.label: meridiano
options.note: The cognate; removes the echo and ends the verse on the Latin's own cadence, but 'meridiano' today is first a line on a map.

decisions.why: verúmtamen ('but yet, nevertheless') renders πλήν and recurs in the psalter (31:6, 38:6–7, 38:12, 48:16, 61:5–6, 61:10, 67:22, 72:18, 84:10, 139:14), so it wants one word. MS1932 drops it ('E tu').

options.label: Todavia,
options.note: Draft. Current, a little grave, four syllables like the Latin word.

options.label: Contudo,
options.note: Same sense, but here it piles up 'Contudo, com… contemplarás'.

options.label: Mas
options.note: DRB 'But'. Plainest and weakest; leaves the colon short.

decisions.why: retribútio is neutral — a paying back — and in other psalms it is a good thing (102:2 retributiónes ejus). MS1932 and pt-PT narrow it to 'castigo'; DRB has 'reward'.

options.label: a retribuição
options.note: Draft. The cognate, as neutral as the Latin, and usable where the repayment is good.

options.label: o castigo
options.note: MS1932 and pt-PT. Clearer here, but it says more than the Latin and cannot serve 102:2.

options.label: a paga
options.note: Short, concrete and neutral; slightly colloquial.

decisions.why: The verse turns in the middle: the first half speaks to God (vós), the second to the just man again (tu). In Latin both are 'tu', so the turn is unmarked; in Portuguese 'puseste' and 'pusestes' differ by one consonant, and the ear may miss it. Rule 2 allows naming a subject hidden in the verb ending.

options.label: tu puseste o Altíssimo por teu refúgio

forms.posuisti: tu puseste o Altíssimo por teu refúgio

options.note: Draft, with MS1932 ('Tu puseste o Altíssimo por teu refúgio'). 'tu' makes the turn audible against 'vós' in the first half. 'pôr por' takes the predicate without article.

options.label: puseste o Altíssimo por teu refúgio

forms.posuisti: puseste o Altíssimo por teu refúgio

options.note: Word for word; the turn rests on the -ste ending and on 'teu'.

options.label: tu fizeste do Altíssimo o teu refúgio

forms.posuisti: tu fizeste do Altíssimo o teu refúgio

options.note: DRB 'thou hast made'. More native, keeps the article, but pónere becomes 'fazer'.

decisions.why: tabernáculum (σκήνωμα) is a tent; it recurs for man's dwelling and for God's (14:1 in tabernáculo tuo). One word should serve both.

options.label: da tua tenda
options.note: Draft, with MS1932 and pt-PT. The concrete image, plain.

options.label: do teu tabernáculo
options.note: The cognate; in Portuguese it now means the tabernacle of the altar or of Moses, not a man's tent.

options.label: da tua morada
options.note: DRB 'dwelling'. An abstraction in place of the image.

decisions.why: mandáre + dative + de: 'he has given his angels a charge concerning you' (perfect in the Latin; the LXX has a future). mandáre is the verb of mandáta → mandamentos in the glossary.

options.label: deu ordem aos seus anjos a teu respeito

forms.mandavit: deu ordem aos seus anjos a teu respeito

options.note: Draft. Clear at first hearing; loses the mandáre / mandáta link.

options.label: mandou aos seus anjos acerca de ti

forms.mandavit: mandou aos seus anjos acerca de ti

options.note: MS1932. Keeps the root of 'mandamento'; but 'mandou aos seus anjos' is heard at first as 'sent to his angels'.

decisions.latin: ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum
decisions.why: The man is the subject and the foot the object (offéndere pedem ad: to strike the foot against); 'ne forte' (μήποτε) is 'lest perhaps'. MS1932 and pt-PT make the foot the subject ('para que o teu pé não tropece') and drop 'forte'.

options.label: para que não batas com o teu pé numa pedra

forms.offendas: para que não batas com o teu pé numa pedra

options.note: Draft. Keeps the Latin's subject; 'bater com o pé em' is what a Brazilian says (and avoids the idiom 'bater o pé' = to insist). 'forte' is not rendered.

options.label: para que não venhas a bater com o teu pé numa pedra

forms.offendas: para que não venhas a bater com o teu pé numa pedra

options.note: 'venhas a' renders 'forte'; three syllables over the Latin.

options.label: para que o teu pé não tropece numa pedra

forms.offendas: para que o teu pé não tropece numa pedra

options.note: MS1932 / pt-PT. The most native; changes the subject.

decisions.why: conculcáre, 'to tread under foot, trample', an intensive; it recurs (55:2–3, 56:4, 138:11) mostly with enemies as the ones who trample.

options.label: calcarás aos pés
options.note: Draft, with MS1932 and DRB ('trample under foot'). Keeps the root calc- and the weight of the compound.

options.label: pisarás
options.note: Plainer and shorter; weaker than the Latin compound.

decisions.why: The Latin has liberábo in 90:14 and erípiam in 90:15 — two verbs (the Greek too: ῥύσομαι / ἐξελοῦμαι). MS1932, pt-PT and DRB give both the same word. erípere is 'to snatch out', and it is one of the psalter's commonest prayers (Éripe me), so it needs a word of its own beside liberáre → livrar.

options.label: arrancarei
options.note: Draft. The concrete image of e-rípere; 'na tribulação' just before it supplies the 'from where'. Works at the vós imperative (Arrancai-me).

options.label: libertarei
options.note: Smoother and distinct from 'livrarei'; but it is the cognate of the other verb, liberáre.

options.label: livrarei
options.note: MS1932, pt-PT. Native; erases the Latin's change of verb.

decisions.why: 'With length of days' (DRB), a noun + genitive. Portuguese has no everyday noun for longitúdo in time; MS1932 drops it ('de dias'), pt-PT turns it into an adjective.

options.label: de longos dias
options.note: Draft, with pt-PT. Noun becomes adjective, the image stays; the colon is 3 syllables short by checks.py, accepted.

options.label: de longura de dias
options.note: Word for word and the right length; 'longura' is a dictionary word nobody says.

choices.90:1: The Latin follows the LXX ('in the help', not 'in the shelter'); kept. protectióne → proteção, so that prótegam in 90:14 (protegerei) answers it, as in the Latin. 'Altíssimo' before the mediant is proparoxytone, exactly like 'Altíssimi' in the Latin.
choices.90:2: The quoted man says 'es tu' to God — so 'Vós sois' — and then 'in eum' of God in the third person: the jump is the Latin's and is kept. sperábo in → esperar em (glossary).
choices.90:3: liberávit is a perfect in the Latin (future in the LXX): 'livrou'. 'a verbo áspero' is a hard Septuagintal reading (the LXX read dabar 'word' for deber 'pestilence'); kept as 'da palavra áspera', with MS1932, pt-PT and DRB ('sharp word'). Both cadences are proparoxytone in Portuguese as in Latin (áspero / áspera).
choices.90:4: From here the just man is addressed: tibi, sperábis → te, esperarás (tu). 'sob' rather than 'debaixo de' only for length. sperábis kept as 'esperarás' (not 'te abrigarás', which is the Hebrew).
choices.90:5: Subject moved to the front (the Latin has Scuto … véritas ejus); 'com um escudo' is the ablative of means — MS1932's 'como um escudo' makes it a comparison. véritas → verdade, not the Hebrew-based 'fidelidade'. First colon +3 by checks.py; 'com‿um' runs together in the mouth. 'temor noturno' and not 'terror noturno', which is a medical term. The verse ends on a comma, as in the Latin, because 90:6 depends on it.
choices.90:6: Three hard readings kept: the unnamed 'thing' that walks in the dark, the 'investida' as a terror of its own (the Latin's comma and 'et' kept), and the noonday demon. 'perambula' is the cognate of perambulánte and a current Brazilian word; 'pelas trevas' because 'perambular por' is the natural regency (the Latin has in). Rhyme flag dia / meio-dia accepted — see the decision.
choices.90:7: The subject of appropinquábit is unexpressed in the Latin (MS1932 supplies '(a morte)'); Portuguese leaves it unexpressed too. appropinquáre is the same verb in 90:7 and 90:10 → 'aproximar-se' in both. The first two cola run 2 syllables short of the Latin, within range.
choices.90:8: considerábis → contemplarás (MS1932, pt-PT): 'considerar' in Portuguese is to think over, not to look. Verb moved before its object in the second colon.
choices.90:9: The turn in mid-verse is kept: 'vós sois' to God, 'tu puseste … teu' to the man. In Latin both halves are 'tu' and nothing marks the change; the vós/tu system forces the translator's hand here, and the project's reading (second half to the man) is the one that makes sense of 'refúgium tuum'. MS1932 bridges it with '(disseste)'; not taken.
choices.90:10: Natural order (subject first) in the first colon; the Latin has the verb first. flagéllum → flagelo (DRB 'scourge'): in Portuguese it is both the whip and the calamity, as wide as the Latin.
choices.90:11: mandávit is a perfect (future in the LXX): 'deu ordem'. custodíre → guardar; via → caminho.
choices.90:12: 'In mánibus' has no possessive in the Latin; none supplied (MS1932 and pt-PT add 'suas'). portábunt → levarão ('carregarão' is the more concrete alternative). First colon −2.
choices.90:13: áspide and basilisco kept, with leão and dragão: the Latin's four beasts, not the Hebrew's. Verb moved to the front. leão / dragão echo inside the colon as leónem / dracónem do.
choices.90:14: God speaks (first person) to the end of the psalm, of the man in the third person. 'eu o livrarei' rather than the mesóclise 'livrá-lo-ei' of MS1932: the brief asks for mesóclise only where it is natural, and with six futures in three verses it would not be. liberábo → livrarei matches liberávit → livrou in 90:3.
choices.90:15: Both pointings respected: it sings with the mediant at ‡ (the app) or at *. exáudiam → escutarei (glossary). '-rei' at ‡ and at the end is flagged as a rhyme by checks.py: accepted, because the Latin has the identical echo (exáudiam eum … glorificábo eum). 'cum ipso sum' keeps its order: 'com ele estou'.
choices.90:16: salutáre meum → 'a minha salvação' (glossary, open entry; MS1932, pt-PT, DRB agree). It is the neuter τὸ σωτήριον, 'the saving thing', which the tradition also hears as a person; 'salvação' leaves that open and is not smoothed into 'socorro' or 'Salvador'. It must come out the same in the Nunc dimittis (salutáre tuum). replébo → encherei (not the Hebrew 'saciarei').

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm90.txt. The project reports that it was read against the printed Hetzenauer 1914 (p. 535) and matches word for word; I did not re-read the page.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps090.md. The Douay-Rheims block in that file is the wrong psalm (it shows Vulgate Ps 89: bolls.life numbers DRB by the Hebrew count, parallels.py asks for chapter 90); I fetched chapter 91 by hand into consult/drb-hebrew91-for-ps090.json and used that. Hard readings kept: a verbo áspero, scápulis suis obumbrábit, a negótio perambulánte in ténebris, ab incúrsu et dæmónio meridiáno, áspidem et basilíscum, salutáre meum; the two Latin perfects against the LXX futures (liberávit 90:3, mandávit 90:11). Address: tu for the just man, vós for God in 90:2 and 90:9a, the turn inside 90:9, God in the first person in 90:14–16.
